review_body:
**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

One distinct sprint-state regression is inline. A focused real 1.21.4 protocol client/server head/base comparison reproduces the missing stop action after disabling physics and clearing controls. Dependencies: minecraft-protocol 1.68.0, minecraft-data 3.116.0. No vanilla server or full version suite was run.

Skills used: prismarine-lifecycle-action-review helped separate simulation readiness from outgoing input state; prismarine-geometry-movement-review helped trace the derived sprint state; prismarine-review checked this against the existing feedback.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

Reviewed the current head and all existing discussion. This finding is separate from the existing anonymous-body issue: named scalar enchantment hashes work, but resolving a server-added enchantment throws before hashing. The reproduction used Minecraft protocol 1.68.0, data 3.116.0 and registry 1.12.0, plus the explicit candidate item #184 / node-protodef #177 / ProtoDef #65 heads. No live server was run.

Skills used: prismarine-review guided deduplication against earlier feedback; prismarine-item-inventory-review and prismarine-protocol-data-review guided the registry-packet, item conversion and fallback checks.
prismarine-architecture-review helped trace registry ownership and identify the bounded fallback.

A synchronous stop followed by a same-goal restart can reuse the cancelled walk's promise. I compared the unmodified head and base controllers with an EventEmitter/planner adapter and checked active-join and post-cleanup restart controls. No live server or full suite was run.

Skills used: prismarine-lifecycle-action-review helped test cancellation and promise cleanup ordering; prismarine-geometry-movement-review helped check the caller's walk contract; prismarine-review helped compare current discussions and avoid duplicate feedback.
